title: Remorse-Return History and Its Effect on Marketplace Orders Refunds
content:
**Rule.** On Marketplace Orders, the buyer's remorse-return history is the count of the buyer's return requests over the measure window whose reason is not a seller-fault reason, across all of the buyer's orders. When the history count is at or above the history threshold of 12 before the new request is counted, a first-scan refund is not available: the item refund waits for the received-at-destination scan whatever the delivery option, and a returnless refund is not available either. A history below the threshold changes nothing. Seller-fault returns never count toward the history and are never delayed by it.

**Measure window.** A rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date, inclusive of both ends, over every order of the buyer. A return request counts when its request date falls in the window and its reason is not one of the seller-fault return reasons.

## Condition, judgement, result

| History count before the new request | Return reason of the new request | First-scan refund | Returnless refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 or more | not a seller-fault reason | not available; the item refund waits for the received-at-destination scan | not available |
| 11 or fewer | any | unchanged by this rule | unchanged by this rule |
| any | a seller-fault reason | never delayed by the history | never delayed by the history |

## Points of judgement

- **Which requests are counted?** Every return request of the buyer, on any of the buyer's orders, dated within the 365-day window, whose reason is not a seller-fault reason (seller-fault reasons are defective, damaged in transit, wrong item, not as described and missing parts).
- **Is the new request part of the count?** No. The count is taken before the new request is counted.
- **Hypothetical boundary.** A buyer with 11 qualifying requests in the window is below the threshold, and nothing changes; a buyer with exactly 12 is at it, and a first-scan refund is not available on a new remorse return. A request dated exactly 365 days back, counting the handling date as day one, still falls in the window. The counts are example inputs.
